To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cyclooxygenases (COXs) are the enzymes responsible for prostaglandin (PG) production in parasites, that PGs are important for parasite pathogenesis, and that parasite PGs can modulate immune function.

(1) The eicosanoids produced by parasites are important mediators of pathogenesis and immunoregulation; (2) Parasite eicosanoids are produced from the host's eicosanoid precursors; and (3) Parasites can produce their own eicosanoids from endogenous fatty acids.
parasites produce eicosanoids and these compounds are involved in pathogenesis and immune modulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of eicosanoid biosynthesis in parasites.

the role of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) in the regulation of the host immune response to parasitic infections and the development of immunomodulatory strategies that may be useful for the treatment of parasitic diseases.

the study of the role of eicosanoids in parasite-host interaction, with a focus on the role of prostaglandin E(2) in parasite survival and the role of prostacyclin in parasite-induced vascular changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prostaglandins are important in the pathogenesis and immunoregulation by parasites.
prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) and prostaglandin F2alpha (PGF2alpha) are produced by a variety of parasites and are involved in pathogenesis and/or immunomodulation of the host.
eicosanoid metabolism by parasites may play a role in the pathogenesis of the infection and/or immunomodulation of the host response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eicosanoid pathway is an important one for parasites and may be used for future drug targets and/or vaccine development.
eicosanoids produced by parasites are not only involved in pathogenesis but also in the modulation of the host immune response.
we are working on a novel mechanism of action for a new class of anti-malarials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eicosanoids are not just produced by parasites, but they are produced by many parasites.
eicosanoids are important in parasite pathogenesis, and that they may be useful targets for the development of novel therapies.
prostaglandin E2 and leukotriene B4 are produced by parasites and have important immunomodulatory roles.
